lesson_title: Double Entry and the Accounting Equation
hook_text: Everything you own was paid for from one of two pockets. So was everything a business owns.
clip_script: Start with something you own — say, your bicycle. One question: where did the money for it come from? Either it was YOUR money — saved pocket money, holiday earnings — or it was SOMEBODY ELSE'S money you still have to repay. There is no third option. Everything anyone owns was paid for from one of two pockets: the own-money pocket or the owed-money pocket. A business works identically, only with bigger numbers. What the business owns EQUALS the owner's pocket PLUS the owed pocket. A equals O plus L.
visual_style: Split-screen: a bicycle on one side, a shop on the other; two glowing pockets feeding both, then the equation assembling itself letter by letter.
pacing: Slow build to the two-pocket reveal, snap to the equation at the end.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to see four transactions keep the table level.
